INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 6, 2019

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on June 6, 2019, in
Community Room A, located on the 1st floor of City Hall. Commissioner Willie Agee called the
meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Willie Agee, Chair–Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick–District One
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore–District Three
  Commissioner Fernando Meza–District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director-Parks, Recreation and Library Services
  Michael Davis, Westside Facilities Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia, Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso- District Two

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Patrick made a motion to approve the minutes from April 4, 2019.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Meza, McLemore, and Agee
  Nays: None

Director’s Reports

  None

Verbal Reports

  Michael Davis gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   Graffiti: There was an increase in graffiti at Ashwood and Edward Vincent Jr. Parks.
  There has also been an increase in the areas around Woodworth, Darby Avenue, and
  Dixon Avenue. In District 3, there was increase in graffiti around La Cienega and La Brea
  Avenues. Graffiti was removed from 1,017 in April 2019 and 1,071 in May.

  1
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 6, 2019

  Commissioner Agee stated that he has noticed an increase in graffiti at Edward Vincent Jr.
Park. Director Barnes stated that because summer has begun there has been an increase in
graffiti throughout the city. When reported, the Graffiti Division removes graffiti in 48 hours or less.
Commissioner Meza reported that behind the CVS on Crenshaw there is an abundance of graffiti
that should be removed. Director Barnes will pass the information to the Graffiti Supervisor.

  Michael Davis gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   Summer Day Camp registration started on May 6, 2019. There are a total of four
  sessions. The first session is June 17-28; second session is July 1-12; third session is
  July 15-26; and, the fourth session starts July 29th and ends on August 9th. Four parks will
  be hosting camps this year. Ages 6-14 years have a choice between Darby and Rogers
  Parks. The 3-5 year olds can choose between Lockhaven Community Center and
  Siminski Park. The Commissioners are encouraged to convey this information to their
  community.
   The Swimming Complex opens June 19th and closes September 2nd for General swim. We
  have swimming lessons available for youth ages 7-17 for three sessions. Session 1 is
  from June 26-July 12, Session 2 July17-August 2 and Session 3 August 7-23. We have
  adult swimming lessons, parent and me swimming lessons and family night swim available
  as well.

  Bharat Devlia gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Mother’s Day Spa: a Spa Day was hosted in partnership with the National Conference of
  Negro Women and the El Camino College Cosmetology. The seniors were treated to
  prewashed hairstyling, manicures and massages, facial and makeup services. It was a
  wonderful experience.
   California Strawberry Festival: A group of 45 seniors traveled to Oxnard, California for a
  fun filled day of picking strawberries, music, activities and food.
   Senior Center Food Menu: The Inglewood Senior Center has a new food menu with the
  California Nutrition program. We are excited about the new menu. The quality of food has
  improved.

  Director Barnes stated that the Department is pleased with the new food vendor. Mr. Devlia
was very instrumental in getting the new vendor settled in the facility. We are pleased to offer a
quality product to our seniors.

Director’s Report

  Sabrina Barnes presented a staff report recommending that the Park and Recreation
Commission Receive and File a report payment for unforeseen and necessary public safety related
work performed at Ashwood Park in order to complete the renovation project. Director Barnes

  2
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 6, 2019

stated that the grand opening for Ashwood Park was extremely well received. As the project was
ending heavy rain caused delays and structural damage. Some structures were repaired and other
areas were improved for public safety (ADA regulations as an example). Additional funds in the
amount of $200,000 will be paid to the contractor for the extra work; bringing the cost to 1.6 million
dollars. Other neighborhood parks that need renovations are expected to be similar in price.

  Commissioner Patrick made a motion to receive and file a staff report regarding payment
in the amount of approximately $200,000 for unforeseen and necessary public safety related work
performed at Ashwood Park in order to complete the renovation project. Commissioner McLemore
seconded and the motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Meza, McLemore, and Agee
  Nays: None

  Sabrina Barnes presented a verbal report regarding Measure A and Prop 68 Funding and
the County Wide Needs Assessment. Director Barnes stated that in 2016 there was a needs
assessment completed. The community was invited to speak on what they thought was needed at
the parks. A list of 10 projects was established. Measure A and Prop 68 was approved and the
monies are becoming available to various cities per capita. $570,000 has been allocated to the
City of Inglewood from Measure A. The list was previously reviewed and some items have been
completed since 2016. Items include: baseball field at Darby Park has been refurbished,
renovating Ashwood Park with a splash pad, we have Wi-Fi at the major parks, and the tennis
courts at Edward Vincent and Rogers Parks are in process of being renovated. The multi-purpose
field at Edward Vincent Park, renovation at Center Park and the interior and walking path at Darby
Park has also been completed. The money will become available again in November. The plan is
to use those funds for the upgrading of the restrooms. Proposition 68 will also have funds
available soon. Center Park’s renovations were funded by Proposition 68. We will be going to
Council about completion of tennis courts at Edward Vincent Park.

  Commissioner Agee inquired about funds for a new sign at the Willie Agee Playhouse.
Director Barnes stated that monies have been requested in the budget for air conditioning and
signage at the Playhouse. Commissioner Patrick asked if the Measure A and Prop 68 funds are
available immediately or disbursed as needed. Director Barnes stated that $570,000 was recently
released and is now available. Another batch of money will be available in November.

Public Comments

  Mr. Hawthorne presented information to the Commission and the Director. He asked that
they read the information at their leisure and requested a meeting with Director Barnes and Teresa
Estrada.

  3
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 6, 2019

  Shelli Boone of the Willie Agee Playhouse presented the Commission with flyers on a
workshop that will be held at the Willie Agee Playhouse. Commissioner Patrick asked for details
on the “set” workshop. It is a workshop on how the build a set for a play from scratch and to also
foster jobs behind the scene.

  Stewart Bailey stated that the Department is doing a wonderful job.

  Mike Asfall stated that there was an issue with a neighborhood gang. The Police came out
to Champions Field and the issue was resolved. He noted that the Recreation staff are younger
generation(s) who may feel intimidation from older more aggressive community members and
suggests that the Department hire more mature staff to enforce rules and regulations. He also
stated that the fencing at Champion’s Field needs to be prepared. Director Barnes stated that
there is request in place when more patrolling is needed and hopes that the community will assist
be calling the police when issues arise.

Commissioners Comments

  None.

The next meeting will be held July11, 2019 at 6:00 p.m. With no further comments the meeting was
adjourned at 6:34 p.m.
